root_cause.text: The `__do_adjtimex` function incorrectly references the global `tk_core` instead of the passed auxiliary timekeeper (`tkd`) when calling `tk_update_leap_state_all`, causing the leap state update to target the wrong timekeeper.
root_cause.evidence: The patch modifies line 2738 in `kernel/time/timekeeping.c`, changing `tk_update_leap_state_all(&tk_core)` to `tk_update_leap_state_all(tkd)`. The CVE description confirms that when `__do_adjtimex` was introduced to handle adjtimex for any timekeeper, this reference to `tk_core` was not updated.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix incorrect call to tk_update_leap_state_all in __do_adjtimex by passing the local tkd pointer instead of the global tk_core.
intent_record.what: Changed argument to tk_update_leap_state_all from &tk_core (global timekeeper structure) to tkd (local pointer to struct tk_data).
intent_record.how: This ensures that the leap state update is applied to the specific tk_data instance being adjusted, rather than always using the global tk_core, which could lead to incorrect leap second handling.
